title: Inspired by Interstellar
caption: The Milky Way arching between two telescopes, La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The band of the Milky Way blazes across the sky and forms a bridge between two telescopes at ESO's La Silla Observatory. The ESO 3.6-meter telescope stands on the left and the Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope on the right. In the upper right corner the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, a pair of nearby galaxies, sit together above the galactic plane.
The bright red splash at the center of the frame is the Gum Nebula. In the lower left, a particularly bright dot is the planet Jupiter.

ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek took this panorama. He said he had wondered whether the colors of the Universe could be captured without complicated equipment, and he was first inspired by one of the posters for Christopher Nolan's film Interstellar. He added that at La Silla it is possible to feel, and to photograph, interstellar moments.

understand.summary: A ground-based panoramic photograph by Petr Horálek for ESO, taken in visible light. The photographer set out to work without complicated equipment. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the red of the Gum Nebula and the brightness of the Milky Way are stronger here than a person would see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture carries the title Inspired by Interstellar. ESO calls La Silla photogenic from every angle, including creative viewpoints such as this panoramic one.
alt: A panoramic view of the Milky Way arching between two telescopes, with a red nebula in the middle of the sky, two small galaxies in the upper right and a bright dot in the lower left.
